messages:
jordan: heads up — seeing a 2-3x tail latency spike on the MoE job during peak traffic this morning. looks like all-to-all stalls after expert swap. attaching quick traces, any obvious suspects?
lee: can you paste the perf snippet? also which model and nnodes?
jordan: model: mixmoe-30B, 8xA100(80). traces: nccl alltoall stalls ~200-400ms occasional, compute stays low during that window. KV cache miss rate up ~12% (was 1-2%).
sam: 12% KV miss is huge — are we invalidating prefixes accidentally? any recent cache key changes?
jordan: no config changes. rollout yesterday swapped kernel selection patch (prefers fast fused-gemm for fp16). wondering if kernel change shifted staleness pattern and increased routing entropies.
aline: can you drop the microtrace from the runtime? the alltoall timeline + kernel queue lengths.
jordan: pasted below:
```
[GPU0] alltoall start 14:32:11.923 duration 312ms
[GPU0] kernel: fused_gemm_fp16 launch queued 8ms, run 11ms
[GPU1] alltoall start 14:32:11.925 duration 298ms
[GPU2] alltoall start 14:32:11.927 duration 319ms
[Runtime] token routing imbalance: max fanout=128, median fanout=18
[KV] lookup miss 12% (prefixsweep job id=874)
```
maria: median fanout 18 seems okay, but max 128 screams hotspot. if one batch has many tokens mapped to same expert group we get huge skew -> long alltoall.
ben: agree. two quick ideas: 1) apply soft-routing cap (limit top-k per-token) 2) stagger alltoall (wavefront scheduling across TP ranks) to smooth peaks.
lee: ben — staggering might interact with current batching heuristics. we already have continuous batching based on sequence length; delaying a batch could blow latency SLO. need a simulation.
athan (ops-bot): deploy-bot: canary of kernel-select v2 rolled back at 14:05 by autorevert due to error rate. fallback still running on 6 nodes though.
jordan: interesting — so partial rollout. might be mixed kernel versions across cluster -> incompatible performance characteristics for NCCL.
sam: mixed kernels + mixed quantization codepaths could change compute time distribution, causing alltoall to wait on slow ranks. we should snapshot kernel variant per rank in the traces.
aline: also check whether KV cache eviction was correlated with rollout window — evictions could increase routing variance because cold tokens replicate to more experts.
jordan: pulled KV eviction logs: evictions spike at 14:30 correlates exactly with tail. remote KV miss fetch adds 6-9ms per token, which amplifies routing variance when combined with alltoall.
maria: concrete next steps: (a) gather per-rank kernel version + queue depth (b) add routing fanout histogram sampling to telemetry (c) run offline sim with our batching heuristic but inject a few high-fanout synthetic requests to see tail.
ben: i'll prototype a soft-cap on per-token fanout in the runtime; will be opt-in flag so we can test on canary. lowers max from 128 -> 32 and stats routing approximation.
lee: i'll run a microbench of staggered alltoall (wavefront scheduling) on 8x node cluster, measure added latency vs reduced max alltoall time. schedule for today afternoon.
sam: if mixed kernel rollout is root cause we need to make kernel selection deterministic at rollout boundaries or ensure per-model kernel compatibility. add to postmortem.
jordan: thanks. leaving a note: if we hit this again, temp mitigation is to route heavy-fanout requests to dedicated experts pool (isolated), or fail fast.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: new ticket created #INC-2026 linking traces and KV evict dump.
maria: tagging @ml-evals to produce a small adversarial prompt set that triggers high fanout so we can reproduce locally.
jordan: great — will follow up with results. :eyes:
